Medical Necessity Cervical Disc Arthroplasty Aetna considers the following Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved prosthetic intervertebral discs medically necessary for the treatment of skeletally mature persons with symptomatic cervical degenerative disc disease or herniated disc at 1 level (also see Additional Notes section): Bryan Cervical Disc and member is 21 years of age or older; Mobi-C and member is at least 21 years and not older than 67 years of age; Prestige Cervical Disc, Prestige LP Cervical Disc and member is at least 21 years and not older than 78 years of age; PCM (Porous Coated Motion) and member is less than or equal to 65 years of age; ProDisc-C, ProDisc-C Vivo, ProDisc-C SK Total Disc Replacement and member is less than or equal to 70 years of age; Secure-C Artificial Cervical Disc and member is at least 21 years and not older than 60 years of age; Simplify Cervical Artificial Disc and member is less than 70 years of age; Synergy Artificial Cervical Disc and member is at least 18 years and not older than 70 years; Or at 2 contiguous levels (also see Additional Notes section): Mobi-C and member is at least 21 years and not older than 67 years of age; Prestige LP Cervical Disc and member is at least 21 years and not older than 78 years of age; Simplify Cervical Artificial Disc and member is less than 70 years of age; Prodisc-C Vivo and Prodisc-C SK and member is at least 18 years and less than 70 years of age. From C3 to C7, when all of the following criteria are met (also see Additional Notes section): All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out; and Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and Imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI) indicate: Nerve root or spinal cord compression at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; or Central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe (not mild or mild to moderate); and There is no radiologic evidence of segmental instability; and Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (see Note below for details and reasons to waive conservative treatment); and Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression; and Member does not have a diagnosis of osteoporosis or osteopenia, and for members 60 years of age and older, member had a DEXA scan confirming T score of - 1.0 or higher within the past year. Aetna considers the following medically necessary (also see Additional Notes section): Subsequent placement of a second artificial cervical disc at a level contiguous to a previous placed artificial disc when criteria for artificial discs are met; Concurrent or planned sequential artificial cervical disc replacement with prior or planned cervical spinal fusion at adjacent levels for the management of cervical spinal pathology when criteria for artificial discs and/or fusion surgery are met. Aetna considers artificial cervical discs experimental, investigational, or unproven for persons with prior disc replacement if the new request would result in more than 2 contiguous disc replacement levels from C3 to C7. Note : Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression. The member should participate in physical therapy for the entire required duration of conservative management (six weeks). Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history. The requirement for a trial of conservative measures may be waived in any of the following situations indicating need for urgent intervention: Spinal cord compression (this does not include nerve root compression); Stenosis causing myelopathy; Stenosis causing severe weakness of the muscle(s) innervated by nerves at the requested surgical level(s) (graded 4 minus or less on MRC scale (see Appendix)) (Note: 4 minus strength describes muscle activation that is beyond antigravity (3/5) and produces motion against only slight resistance and fails against moderate resistance); Progressive neurological deficit on serial examinations; A discharge note from a physical therapist documenting lack of utility of further physical therapy. Aetna recognizes that revision or removal surgery for disc arthroplasty may be medically necessary, though infrequently, and any case would need documentation as to the reasons for failure of the prior surgery and the potential benefits of the proposed revision surgery. Experimental, Investigational, or Unproven Aetna considers all of the following (not an all-inclusive list) experimental, investigational, or unproven because there is insufficient evidence of their effectiveness: Lumbar partial disc prosthetics (e.g., Nubac, DASCOR Disc Arthroplasty System) Lumbar prosthetic intervertebral discs at more than one level M6-C Artificial Cervical Disc MOTUS lumbar total joint replacement implant (3Spine) / posterior vertebral joint replacement (3Spine) Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting for intervertebral disc regeneration Total posterior spine (TOPS) System. For lumbar disc arthroplasty, if member is diabetic, their HbA1c should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to surgery. For purposes of this policy, Aetna will consider the official written report of complex imaging studies (e.g., CT, MRI, myelogram). If the operating surgeon disagrees with the official written report, the surgeon should document that disagreement. The surgeon should discuss the disagreement with the provider who did the official interpretation, and there should also be a written addendum to the official report indicating agreement or disagreement with the operating surgeon. The imaging should be performed within the past year, or after the onset of the current constellation of symptoms or any relevant surgical procedures, whichever is sooner. For purposes of this policy, any nerve root or spinal cord compression meets criteria regardless of the degree of stenosis on the imaging report. Terms such as mass effect, impingement, abutment, effacement, indentation, flattening, or displacement do not substitute for compression.
